title: How to Prepare a Packaging Design Project
h1: How to prepare a packaging design project
description: What a packaging designer needs: product details, dieline from your manufacturer, required label information, shelf context, print method, mockups and proofs.
intro: Packaging has to do several jobs at once. It protects the product, carries required information, stands out on a shelf or in an online listing and reflects your brand. It also has to fit the exact structure your manufacturer can produce. Designers can only deliver print-ready packaging if they receive the right technical details and content. This article explains what to prepare before hiring a packaging designer and how to avoid the most expensive mistakes.

faq.a: A flat template from the manufacturer showing the exact shape, folds, cuts and glue areas of the package.

faq.q: Can the designer create the dieline?
faq.a: Some can, but it should always be confirmed by your manufacturer before final artwork.

faq.q: What information must appear on the label?
faq.a: It depends on the product and country. Check the rules for your category and market.
It helps you judge the design and is useful for online listings before production samples exist.

faq.q: Should I order a physical sample?
faq.a: Yes. Colors, folds and readability are best checked on a real printed sample.
